title.narrative: Readiness actions for potential new population movements in Oromia for integrated Emergency WASH, S/NFI, and MPC assistance (Fentale, East Wollega H/Guduru Wollega Zone)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposed anticipatory action aims to strengthen preparedness and deliver timely, safe, and dignified humanitarian assistance to 42,800 people affected by conflict and natural disasters—primarily newly displaced populations—in the Oromia region.ltbrgtThe intervention uses an integrated approach, with ZOA leading Emergency Shelter/Non-Food Items (ES/NFI), Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH), and Multi-Purpose Cash (MPC) assistance, while MCMDO, a local partner, leads Nutrition and Health support.ltbrgtKey project activities include:ltbrgtltbgtWASHlt/bgt: Rehabilitating water schemes, providing water treatment chemicals, distributing hygiene kits (including MHM kits), conducting hygiene promotion, and building emergency latrines.ltbrgtltbgtES/NFIlt/bgt: Prepositioning and distributing emergency shelter and essential non-food items to protect displaced populations.ltbrgtltbgtMPClt/bgt: Offering flexible cash assistance to cover urgent needs like WASH, shelter, and livelihoods, particularly for those not reached through in-kind support.ltbrgtThree woredas_Amaya (Southwest Shewa), Abe Dongoro (Horo Guduru), and Goro Dola (East Borena)—are tentatively identified as project sites. Final locations will be based on real-time needs, assessed through displacement triggers (e.g., 1,000+ households affected) and coordinated with government bodies, UNOCHA, and partners.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtltbgtUpdate 1: lt/bgtDepending on the cluster endorsement ZOA started responding on the earthquake response for IDP at Fentale Woreda in East Shewa Zone, Oromia Region. ltbrgtFentale has been experiencing significant seismic activity since September 27, 2024, linked to the Fentale volcanic complex. The most severe earthquake, with a magnitude of 5.8, struck on December 4, 2024, causing widespread structural damage in seven kebeles—five of which were heavily affected.ltbrgtAn initial 20,325 people (3,525 households) were displaced from kebeles including Benti, Kobo, Deka Edu, Haro Kersa, and Debiti. As of early 2025, the total number of internally displaced people (IDPs) has reached approximately 32,620 (5,500 households), now residing in six IDP sites: Banti, Kobo, Dheka Hedu, Boda, Gelcha, and Ilala.ltbrgtThe earthquakes and a recent volcanic eruption have destroyed homes, health centers, schools, roads, and livelihoods, severely disrupting daily life and transportation. While seismic activity has recently decreased, the situation remains unpredictable. Affected communities are in urgent need of humanitarian assistance.ltbrgt lt/pgt
